title: Build Plan
description: Canonical state file for the requirements-to-build layer: .sfskills/builds/<build-id>/plan.json. Contract: standards/build-orchestration.md (v1, 2026-09-05) sections 2-5 and 8. Every agent in the loop reads this file before acting and updates only the fields it owns; the human-readable views (PLAN.md, CLARIFICATIONS.md) are rendered from it by scripts/build_plan.py, which is also the only writer of human_gates[].

build_id.description: Kebab-case build identifier. Matches the directory name under .sfskills/builds/.

title.description: One-line human title for the build.

version.description: Plan version. Section 3: re-planning after a rejected plan gate is a new version (version + 1); the superseded plan is pushed into history[].

status.description: Build lifecycle status. Section 3 stage table: intake -> clarifying -> planned -> verified|plan-rejected -> approved (G2) -> building -> done (last milestone gate approved).

build_mode.description: design-only = the build has no org target, so every step must be owned by an agent with requires_org: false (the metadata-builder default owner for metadata step types). org-connected = an org alias is available, so org-requiring designer agents may own steps. Set by scripts/build_plan.py init (--org-alias switches it to org-connected); enforced by validate and by the plan-verifier's executability lens.

org.description: Present only when build_mode is org-connected. The layer never deploys; the alias is what org-requiring agents read metadata through.

updated.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp of the last mutation. scripts/build_plan.py does not maintain it (rendered views must stay byte-deterministic); agents may.

source_path.description: Path to the human's verbatim requirement, relative to the build directory. Section 2: requirement.md.

summary.description: One-paragraph restatement of the requirement in the layer's own words.

clarifications.description: Section 1.1 / 3: every question the relevant skills' 'Questions to Ask Before Configuring' tables say must be asked, deduped, each with a proposed default. Never capped.

id.description: Q1, Q2, ... Stable across renders; CLARIFICATIONS.md round-trips on this id.

kind.description: blocking = G1 cannot pass until answered or explicitly deferred.

why.description: Why the answer changes the build. Usually lifted from the source skill's Questions-to-Ask table.

proposed_default.description: The default the human may accept in one action.

answer.description: The human's answer. 'DEFER: <reason>' is the explicit deferral form for a blocking question.

source_skill.description: Skill id whose Questions-to-Ask table produced this question.

group.description: Optional grouping key, e.g. 'objects-and-fields', 'access', 'sla'. scripts/build_plan.py render groups the questions under a '### <group>' heading inside Blocking / Informational, in first-appearance order, with ungrouped questions last under 'Other'. A grouping key, not a step type: nothing validates it against the section 4 table.

owner_role.description: Who in the requester's organisation can actually answer this, e.g. 'Data steward', 'Support manager'. Rendered as one line so the human can route the question rather than guess.

answer_shape.description: What a usable answer looks like, e.g. 'the picklistValues blocks per record type'. Rendered as one line; it is what stops a one-word answer that does not unblock the step.

also_asked_by.description: Other skill ids whose Questions-to-Ask table asked the same question before dedup. source_skill is the one the wording came from; this is the rest of the evidence that the question is not invented.

default_source.description: Where proposed_default came from, e.g. 'skill-guidance', 'requirement', 'none'. 'none' means the layer had no basis for a default and the human must supply the answer.

assumptions.description: Everything the plan takes as true without confirmation, including accepted defaults for unanswered informational questions.

verdict.description: fit = standard configuration covers it; partial = configuration plus work; gap = nothing on the platform covers it as asked.

decisions.description: Section 1.2: each decision cites the decision-tree branch that resolved it, or — when no tree covers the choice — the skill reference that did, in source_reference, with adr_required: true.

decision_tree.description: Path under standards/decision-trees/. Validated to exist on disk.

branch.description: The tree step that resolved the choice, e.g. 'Q3'. scripts/build_plan.py validate reads decision_tree off disk and ERRORs unless the tree actually heads a step with this id ('Q3. <question>', '## Q3', '**Q3**', 'Q3 —' or an explicit anchor) — a branch id nobody can find in the tree is a citation of something that was never read.

branch_quote.description: The branch text, quoted verbatim from the tree. Rendered as a sub-bullet under the PLAN.md decisions table so a reader can check the branch says what the decision says without opening the tree.

source_reference.description: Repo-relative path to the skill reference that resolved this choice when no decision tree covers it (build-planner Step 4 / build-planner step 4). Validated to exist on disk. Cite this instead of stretching a tree branch to cover a decision it does not make; a decision resolved this way sets adr_required: true.

adr_required.description: True when the choice was not settled by a decision-tree branch and deserves its own architecture decision record. Rendered as the ADR column of the PLAN.md decisions table.

consequences.description: What this decision costs or forecloses. Rendered as a sub-bullet under the PLAN.md decisions table.

milestones.description: Ordered M1..Mn. Each milestone ends at a human acceptance gate (G3).

steps.description: Exactly the ids of the steps whose 'milestone' is this id.

acceptance_tests.description: Cross-step checks the milestone verifier runs. Section 5: every milestone has at least one.

status.description: pending -> building (set when the first step starts) -> verified (milestone-verifier) -> accepted (G3 approved) | rejected (G3 rejected; the build stays 'building' and the milestone is reworked).

report_path.description: reports/MILESTONE-<id>-REPORT.md once the verifier has run.

steps.description: Section 4: the unit of build. Exactly one owning run-time agent and one step type per step.

human_gates.description: Section 3: 'clarifications' (G1), 'plan' (G2), 'milestone:<id>' (G3, one per milestone) and 'step:<step-id>' (one per step with human_gate: true). Agents never approve a gate; scripts/build_plan.py gate is the only writer.

artefacts_root.description: Directory, relative to the build directory, under which every step writes artefacts/<step-id>/. Section 2: 'artefacts'.

docs.description: Rendered / appended human-readable views, relative to the build directory. Never hand-edit a rendered view (section 2).

history.description: Superseded plan versions (section 3). Written only by scripts/build_plan.py gate on a rejected plan gate.

verification.description: Section 7: written by .claude/workflows/plan-verify.js synthesis. Open shape so lenses can extend.

acceptanceTest.description: Section 5. checker/command declare a command; xml and manifest are the always-on structural checks; manual is a checklist line the human ticks at the milestone gate.

command.description: Required for type checker and command. Stdlib-only and read-only: a checker command must be 'python3 skills/<domain>/<slug>/scripts/check_*.py ...' and the file must exist; a command test must start with 'python3 ' and name a path in the repo or under the build directory. scripts/build_plan.py validate rejects anything matching the deploy/fetch/shell deny-list (sf ... deploy, sfdx, force:source:deploy, curl, wget, pipe-to-shell, bash -c, python -c, rm -rf, git push).

scope.description: Checker tests only; default 'step'. Declared INTENT, not a path source: step-tester runs the command string verbatim and substitutes no path, so the tree the checker reads is the one written into the command's own --manifest-dir. 'step' declares that the command carries --manifest-dir artefacts/<step-id>/ (the one step's artefacts); 'build' declares that it carries --manifest-dir artefacts (the whole artefacts root), which is the only honest scope for a cross-referential checker — one that asserts relationships across components a single step does not own (check_escalation_rules.py, check_omni_channel_routing_setup.py, check_list_views_and_compact_layouts.py, check_permission_set_architecture.py). The declared scope and the command's --manifest-dir must name the same tree; scripts/build_plan.py validate WARNs on the disagreement, and WARNs when one of those four checkers is declared with step scope on a routing/sla/access step. At milestone level every checker test is build-scoped by definition, so scope is redundant there.

run.description: Section 8: every agent invocation in the loop is recorded here with its envelope path. Re-running a step appends; it never overwrites history.

type.description: Section 4 step-type table. Adding a type = one new row there plus a roster agent.

agent.description: Owning run-time agent id. Must exist with class: runtime and status != deprecated (section 8).

skills.description: Skill ids the agent must read. Must resolve to skills/<domain>/<slug>/SKILL.md.

inputs.description: Free-form inputs the runner hands the owning agent.

outputs.description: Artefact paths, relative to the build directory, under artefacts/<step-id>/.

depends_on.description: Step ids that must be 'documented' before this step is runnable. Must form a DAG.

status.description: Section 4 state machine: pending -> running -> built -> tested -> documented, with failed and blocked as side exits.

human_gate.description: True if this step needs its own human sign-off beyond the milestone gate.

blocked_reason.description: Required when status is blocked. 'skill-gap' is the reserved reason for section 8's deepen-a-skill signal.
